name: Synthetic Network
what_it_is: A Docker-based framework that places containers on a synthetic network whose conditions (bandwidth, latency, packet loss, jitter, reordering) can be manipulated at runtime. The traffic-shaping engine is a Rust userspace proxy called Rush (a Snabb port), controlled via a REST/JS API or a web GUI.
components: rush — Rust userspace packet-processing proxy that bridges the real network interface to a veth pair and enforces QoS rules
frontend — Node.js web server (port 80/3000) exposing a GUI and REST API to read/write the QoS configuration and traffic profiles
setup.sh — container entrypoint that wires up the veth pair, installs default routes, launches rush and the frontend, then executes the user's test entry point
syntheticnet Docker image — Node 12 base with iproute2, ethtool, iperf3, tcpdump, net-tools, and Rust nightly toolchain
syntheticnet:vnc / syntheticnet:chrome optional images — add TigerVNC + ratpoison; chrome variant includes Chromium for browser-level network testing
protocols: Any TCP/UDP/IP traffic routed through the synthetic interface is conditioned
Per-flow rules can target UDP specifically (flow matching by protocol field)
HTTP REST API on port 80/3000 for programmatic control (separate from the conditioned interface)
Chrome DevTools remote protocol available in chrome image (port unaffected by conditioning)
measurement: Profiles expose per-flow packet counts readable via the JS API (synthnet.profiles.ingress.get())
Host-side tools available inside container: tcpdump, iperf3, netstat, ping
configuration: QoS spec file at /opt/etc/synthetic_network.json (JSON); mounted or baked into image
Fields per direction (ingress/egress): rate (bps integer), loss (float 0–1), latency (ms), jitter (ms), jitter_strength (float), reorder_packets (bool)
default_link block applies to all traffic; flows array adds per-protocol/per-flow overrides
Runtime updates via JS API: synthnet.default_link.ingress.rate(n); await synthnet.commit()
SYNTHETIC_NETWORK env var sets the subnet (default 10.77.0.0/16)
ENTRY env var overrides the test entry point (default /opt/bin/entry)
USE_VNC env var wraps ENTRY with VNC server
TESTHOST env var injects an /etc/hosts entry into the container
Reload config without restart: send SIGHUP to the rush process
fault_injection: Packet loss: loss field (e.g. 0.02 = 2%) on ingress or egress independently
Latency: latency field (milliseconds) added to every packet
Jitter: jitter + jitter_strength fields for variable delay
Bandwidth cap: rate field (bits per second) for ingress and egress independently
Per-protocol flow rules allow targeting UDP vs TCP independently
All faults can be changed live at runtime via API without restarting the container
modes: Interactive debug mode: make run-interactive (bash shell inside container on synthetic network)
Chrome/VNC mode: make run-chrome — Chromium inside VNC accessible at localhost:5901, GUI at localhost:3000
Minimal/headless mode: syntheticnet:minimal image — no GUI, config from /opt/etc/synthetic_network.json only
Scripted mode: JS client library synthetic-network/frontend controls conditions programmatically
constraints: Container MUST run with --privileged flag — setup.sh uses ip link/ip route/ip address to manipulate kernel networking
Container MUST be connected to a Docker network created with --subnet matching SYNTHETIC_NETWORK (default 10.77.0.0/16)
Only traffic routed through the synthetic Docker network is conditioned; control-plane traffic (API, VNC, Chrome remote) uses the default Docker network and is unaffected
Minimal image has no GUI — network conditions must be set via pre-baked /opt/etc/synthetic_network.json or SIGHUP reload; live scripting requires the full image
Rush is built with Rust nightly toolchain; reproducible builds require vendored dependencies (vendor/ directory checked in)
No docker-compose file provided — orchestration is done via bare docker network create + docker create/run make targets
docker_services: syntheticnet — main image (Node 12 + Rush + frontend web UI)
syntheticnet:vnc — adds TigerVNC + ratpoison window manager
syntheticnet:chrome — adds Chromium on top of vnc image
syntheticnet:minimal — Rush only, no frontend GUI
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml — no multi-container orchestration example provided
No Kubernetes/CNI integration — designed exclusively for Docker networks
No built-in test assertions or pass/fail framework — measurement is read-only profiles; evaluation logic must be provided by the user's ENTRY script
No Windows container support — Linux kernel networking (iproute2, veth) required
